description: Siemens SIPROTEC 4 7SA613 distance zones (Z1, Z2, Z3, Z4, Z5, Z1B) as a DIGSI 4 setting sheet prints them (address | name | value | range). Catalog-only, verified subset: the per-zone Op. mode (status and direction, with 1201 FCT Distance), R(Zn) ph-ph, X(Zn), RE(Zn) ph-E, the RE/RL - XE/XL compensation, the CT / VT ratings (units printed in the range column) and the line data. Every zone delay setting cell is blank or 'Infinity': no delay is assumed. The impedance basis and the characteristic are not stated and are not assumed; Z5's negative reactance reach, Z1's zone-reduction angle and the distance angle (inclined resistance boundaries) are preserved as capability gaps.
interpretation_notes: The zones are the sheet's Z1, Z2, Z3, Z4, Z5 and Z1B parameter groups (addresses 13xx); each zone's state and direction come from its own 'Op. mode' setting, with the distance function itself (1201 FCT Distance) switched on.
The sheet states impedances in ohms but not whether they are primary or secondary ohms, and does not name the zone characteristic: neither is assumed (Missing).

Every zone delay (T1-1phase, T1-multi-phase, T2..., T3 DELAY, T4 DELAY, T5 DELAY, T1B...) has a blank setting cell or 'Infinity'. A blank cell is not a delay, the 'Infinity' in the range column is not a setting, and an 'Infinity' setting is not a finite delay: no delay is assumed, and the document notes' timers are not used.

The polygon's resistance boundaries are inclined at the distance angle (1211); the current model cannot draw an inclined boundary, so that setting is preserved with every zone. No left (-R) boundary is stated.

zone_preserved.reason: The polygon's resistance boundaries are inclined at the distance angle. The current model draws resistance limits as vertical lines, so this geometry cannot be represented; the setting is preserved, not approximated.
Zone 1's zone-reduction angle is preserved as stated; the current model cannot apply it to the drawn boundary.
The reactance reach of non-directional Zone 5 in the reverse direction (X-). The canonical zone carries one reactive reach (X+ is mapped); the reverse reach cannot be represented and is preserved.

mappings.note: CT secondary as printed; the range column states the unit (AMP).
Rated primary voltage; the range column states kV (converted to volts).
Line length as printed; its unit is the sheet's 'Distance Unit'.
The zone's own Op. mode: Inactive puts it out of service; a direction puts it in service while the distance function (1201) is ON.

The zone is stated as X and R limits (X(Zn), R(Zn) ph-ph, RE(Zn) ph-E), not as a polar reach. Its resistance boundaries are inclined at the distance angle, which this representation cannot carry (preserved with the zone).
X(Z5)+: the forward reactance reach of Zone 5. Its reverse reach X(Z5)- is preserved with the zone.
R(Zn) ph-ph, the phase-phase resistance reach, as printed.
RE(Zn) ph-E, the phase-earth resistance reach, as printed. Not drawn by the phase-phase engine.
